subject: OpticTech account opportunity alignment & timeline
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena@optictech.com>, Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@optictech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: OpticTech post-call: alignment on pain, goals, and proposed next steps

Thanks again for carving out time today — appreciated the clear description of how RAG queries and nightly batch embeddings are driving costs and latency for your customer-facing search experience. Quick summary from our side and concrete next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Key pain points you called out:
- High token costs for nightly re-indexing and embedding refreshes (spike midnights UTC).
- Latency-sensitive search traffic during business hours (p95 ~ 420ms, target < 200ms).
- Concern about data residency and audit logs for PCI-adjacent metadata.

Goals you want to hit by Q4:
1) Reduce per-query inference spend by 30% while keeping relevance steady.
2) Move RAG embedding refresh off peak hours and enable incremental updates.
3) Have a clear path to Dedicated capacity for steady throughput with SLA.

What Redwood can do (initial proposal):
- Dedicated pilot: reserved GPUs + autoscale buffer for peak reindex windows.
- Optimize batching + KV prefix caching for search traffic to reduce per-token cost.
- Private deployment checklist (VPC + audit logs) for regulated metadata flows.

Immediate next steps (ask):
1) Elena/Carlos: confirm the top 3 datasets you re-index nightly (names + avg tokens per doc) — due Tue 6/23.
2) Ben: I’m attaching the usage export we ran together and a first-draft mutual action plan. Please propose a realistic pilot size and estimated monthly cost delta.
3) Marcus: please include SOC2 evidence stub and an ops-runbook draft for the Dedicated pilot.

Attachments included: [Attachment: optictech_usage_report_q1.csv (CSV, 120KB)], [Attachment: mutual_action_plan_v1.pdf (PDF, 85KB)].

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar hold for a technical pilot design session (30–45m) next week.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199
Redwood Inference
From: Elena Soto <elena@optictech.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@optictech.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OpticTech post-call: alignment on pain, goals, and proposed next steps

Vanessa — thanks for the clear summary. Confirming a few details so your team has what it needs: 

Quick clarifications:
- Nightly re-indexes: docs: customer_profiles, product_catalog, support_faqs. Average token sizes: profiles ~ 3.2k, product_catalog ~ 1.1k, support_faqs ~ 400.
- Peak hours (US/PT): 14:00–18:00 UTC, search p95 spikes align with our morning batch processing.

We’re comfortable with the pilot objectives you outlined. One ask: can Redwood provide a separate rollover window for embedding refreshes (we cannot push to 02:00 UTC due to maintenance windows). Prefer 05:00–07:00 UTC.

I’ve reviewed the mutual action plan briefly — will send detailed comments by EOD Tue. Also flagged SOC2 requirement — we’ll need the certificate and a short note on logs retention policy.

Elena
Head of Data Products, OpticTech
elena@optictech.com

> Thanks again for carving out time today — appreciated the clear description...
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena@optictech.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OpticTech post-call: alignment on pain, goals, and proposed next steps

Elena — quick follow up from infra/solutions perspective. We ran a rough estimate against the usage export Vanessa attached. High level:

- Pilot suggestion: 4x A10G-equivalent GPUs reserved for burstable Dedicated pool (target: 500 concurrent RPS for small-search requests + batch embedding windows).
- Expected delta: ~+12–18% monthly cost for reserved pool vs current on-demand spend, with projected 28–35% reduction in per-query CPU/GPU time due to KV caching and optimized batching.

Technical notes / constraints:
- We can shift embedding refresh to 05:00–07:00 UTC as requested; we’ll also support incremental incremental updates to product_catalog to avoid full re-embeds.
- For data residency: we’ll enable VPC peering and provide audit-log snapshots daily (retention configurable).

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood_quick_pricing_sheet.xlsx (XLSX, 42KB)].

Proposed next milestone: Technical design session Wed 6/24 10:00–10:45 PT — agenda: pilot sizing, QoS profile, fallback policy. Vanessa: can you send a calendar invite? Elena: confirm availability.

—
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena@optictech.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@optictech.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 09:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OpticTech post-call: alignment on pain, goals, and proposed next steps

All — thanks. Elena — 05:00–07:00 UTC works and I’ve penciled in Wed 6/24 10:00 PT for the technical design session (invite sent).

Summary of agreed action items / owners: 
- Elena/Carlos: confirm dataset names and token averages (customer_profiles, product_catalog, support_faqs) — assigned to OpticTech — due Tue 6/23.
- Ben: final pilot sizing + pricing sheet (attach) — due Tue 6/23 EOD.
- Marcus: SOC2 certificate + ops runbook draft and logs-retention options — due Wed 6/24 (bring to the call).
- Vanessa: calendar invite, deck for pilot objectives, and updated mutual action plan (v1 -> v1.1) — will share before the design session.

If there are no objections I’ll mark the pilot MVP as: 2-week Dedicated pilot with 4x reserved GPUs, KV prefix caching enabled, embedding refresh window 05:00–07:00 UTC, with telemetry and cost dashboard access for OpticTech engineers.

Thanks — looking forward to the design session.

—
